Setup

All the functions live in stock_functions.R so this file just loads them and runs them. quantmod and TTR get loaded inside that script.

source("stock_functions.R")

Portfolio

The stock symbols are stored in portfolio.txt, one per line.

symbols <- read_portfolio("portfolio.txt")
symbols
## [1] "AAPL" "MSFT" "NVDA" "AMZN" "TSLA"

Importing the Data

load_stock_data() reads portfolio.txt and downloads daily prices for each symbol from Yahoo Finance (Jan 1 - Dec 31, 2025). Each stock ends up as its own data frame inside a named list.

stocks <- load_stock_data("portfolio.txt", from = "2025-01-01", to = "2026-01-01")

names(stocks)
## [1] "AAPL" "MSFT" "NVDA" "AMZN" "TSLA"
sapply(stocks, class)   # each one is a separate data frame
##         AAPL         MSFT         NVDA         AMZN         TSLA 
## "data.frame" "data.frame" "data.frame" "data.frame" "data.frame"
sapply(stocks, nrow)    # number of trading days per stock
## AAPL MSFT NVDA AMZN TSLA 
##  250  250  250  250  250

Structure of one of the data frames:

str(stocks[[1]])
## 'data.frame':    250 obs. of  7 variables:
##  $ Date    : Date, format: "2025-01-02" "2025-01-03" ...
##  $ Open    : num  249 243 244 243 242 ...
##  $ High    : num  249 244 247 246 244 ...
##  $ Low     : num  242 242 243 241 240 ...
##  $ Close   : num  244 243 245 242 243 ...
##  $ Volume  : num  55740700 40244100 45045600 40856000 37628900 ...
##  $ Adjusted: num  242 242 243 240 241 ...

The data is also saved as CSV files in an output/ folder.

save_stock_data(stocks)

Displaying the Data

Historical data (last 10 trading days)

Same layout as the Historical Data tab on Yahoo Finance, newest day first.

for (sym in names(stocks)) {
  cat("\n\n####", sym, "\n\n")
  print(knitr::kable(display_historical(stocks[[sym]], sym, n = 10),
                     align = "r"))
}

Quote summary

A summary box like the one at the top of a Yahoo Finance stock page. “Period Range” is the lowest low and highest high over the whole year.

for (sym in names(stocks)) {
  cat("\n\n####", sym, "\n\n")
  print(knitr::kable(display_quote_summary(stocks[[sym]], sym)))
}

Statistics

calculate_statistics() works on the daily closing price for each stock: mean, median, mode, standard deviation, min, max, and the latest 20-day and 50-day simple moving averages. calculate_all_statistics() runs it on every stock and puts the results into one table.

stats <- calculate_all_statistics(stocks)
knitr::kable(stats)
Symbol From To Days Mean Median Mode SD Min Max SMA_20_Last SMA_50_Last
AAPL 2025-01-02 2025-12-31 250 232.24 230.00 211 26.47 172.42 286.19 275.47 272.66
MSFT 2025-01-02 2025-12-31 250 464.43 479.69 510 50.52 354.56 542.07 483.41 496.51
NVDA 2025-01-02 2025-12-31 250 153.90 158.79 178 29.77 94.31 207.04 182.50 186.36
AMZN 2025-01-02 2025-12-31 250 217.67 222.12 223 17.10 167.32 254.00 228.77 231.44
TSLA 2025-01-02 2025-12-31 250 356.97 344.04 285 69.98 221.86 489.88 464.70 445.10

A few notes on how these are calculated:

  • Mode - base R doesn’t have a mode function, and closing prices basically never repeat to the exact cent, so prices are rounded to the nearest dollar first and the most common value is taken.
  • SD - sd() gives the sample standard deviation (divides by n - 1).
  • Moving averages - SMA() from the TTR package. The value shown is from the last trading day of the year.

Visualizations

Closing price with moving averages

for (sym in names(stocks)) {
  plot_price_with_ma(stocks[[sym]], sym)
}

Candlestick charts with volume (quantmod)

for (sym in names(stocks)) {
  plot_candlestick(stocks[[sym]], sym)
}

Relative performance of the whole portfolio

Every stock starts at 100 on the first trading day so they can be compared on one chart.

plot_normalized(stocks)
